title: microcharge-heatmap-lens-wires
content:
Summary:

This note captures an iteration of a 'Microcharge Heatmap Lens' — an exploration UI for surfacing token-level cost and latency contributions across invocations. The goal is a compact, explorable surface that answers: which tokens, model variants, or persistent cache hits drive cost and tail latency for a route or customer cohort, and how would configuration changes (batching, quantization, cache policy) shift the economics?

Why different from previous token inspector work:
- Focus on a heatmap-first lens (density + cost intensity) rather than list-based token traces.
- Introduces temporal cohorting (sequence-length slider) and a small-signal simulator to preview changes to batching/quantization.
- Emphasizes compact comparison between two cohorts (e.g., pre/post-rollout or model A vs model B).

Primary personas:
- Platform engineer (SRE / infra) diagnosing regressions in p95 token cost spikes.
- ML engineer validating model quantization rollout impact on unit economics.
- Product/Revenue analyst doing quick attribution across customers/routes.

Top-level UX components (wireframe states):
1) Overview "Lane" (default):
   - Mini-heatmap: X-axis = token position (0..max-seq aggregated buckets), Y-axis = token token-type buckets (system/prompt/context/response) plus a small row for cache-hits. Color = cost-per-token (darker = higher cost). Opacity/height = token frequency.
   - Left rail: route/model selector, cohort selector (time, customer, route, tag), metric toggles (cost / latency / combined score).
   - Top controls: sequence-length slider (cohort the dataset by max_seq bucket), compare toggle (enable side-by-side lane).
   - Mini summary cards (p50 cost/token, p95 latency, estimated units/day).

2) Inspect panel (right side, pivots on selection):
   - Token drill: when the user clicks a heatmap cell, panel shows top example invocations (sampled), a tiny prompt snippet, the token, its average cost contribution, average KV-cache status, % of times it was part of high-p95 events.
   - Suggested actions: quick toggles for hypothetical changes (turn on per-route KV caching, apply static quantization profile, increase batching target), with an instant delta estimate shown next to each suggestion (uses simulation backend).

3) Compare lanes (two heatmaps side-by-side):
   - For comparing model variants, rollout windows, or before/after changes. Diff overlay option: red/green cells show relative delta in cost intensity.

4) Anomaly-explorer mode:
   - Time-series on top showing anomaly flags (sudden hot cells). Clicking a flag zooms to the impacted heatmap buckets and surfaces example invocations.

Interactions / micro-interactions:
- Hover: tooltip with sample count, avg tokens per invocation for that bucket, p95 latency contribution, and sample invocation id link to Logs/Trace.
- Brush-select: select a token-position range or type rows to filter cohorts.
- Relative vs absolute toggle: switch between absolute cost per token vs normalized (percent of invocation cost).
- Snapshot + export: capture a view and export CSV rows for the selected bucket(s).

Wireframe notes (sketches to build in Figma):
- Canvas grid uses thin separators so dense heatmap remains scannable.
- Palette: use color ramp focused on cost intensity (muted blues -> amber -> deep magenta) to avoid red-only alerts.
- Small-multiples compact view for comparing 3+ variants (stacked, compressed rows).

Data model & instrumentation notes (engineering constraints):
- Heatmap aggregation keys: route_id, model_id, model_variant, customer_id (optional), token_position_bucket, token_role (system/prompt/response/context), cache_status (miss/hit/local_kv).
- Each invocation must emit per-token summaries (cost_estimate, latency_ms, kv_flag) but sample at 5% by default to control cardinality. Full capture only on anomaly sampling or user-triggered trace.
- Backend storage: pre-aggregate daily + hourly rollups for quick pivoting. Keep raw sampled rows for 30 days. Maintain separate analytic store for simulation queries (higher QPS).
- Cardinality mitigation: cap customer_id granularity for free-tier customers (roll up to 'bucketed_customer') and surface export-only for high-cardinality cohorts.

Simulation rules for "suggested actions":
- Batching: assume effective latency/cost change curves derived from internal perf table for model_variant and seq_len bucket. Provide conservative and optimistic delta ranges.
- Quantization: use per-model-profile expected token-cost multiplier. Sim results must show uncertainty band.

MVP scope (what we ship first):
- Single-lane heatmap, route and model selector, sequence-length slider, hover tooltips, inspect panel with 3 example invocations and suggested action quick-sim (batching + quantization only), export CSV, compare toggle (two lanes).
- Sampling defaults and backend rollups implemented; retention 30d for raw samples, 90d for rollups.

Nice-to-have (future iterations):
- Live streaming heatmap for tail regression debugging.
- Auto-summaries ("Top 5 token clusters contributing >40% cost for this route").
- Integration with rollout system to automatically propose KV caching or fallback policies for routes showing high token-cost concentration.

Accessibility & performance considerations:
- Render heatmap as canvas with WebGL fallback to avoid DOM explosion for large buckets.
- Colorblind-safe palette and numeric overlays on hover.
- Lazy-load example invocation payloads; preserve privacy by redacting tokens in UI by default (allow show-redacted toggle for authorized users).

Open questions / trade-offs to discuss in the next grooming: 
- Sampling rate defaults: 1% vs 5% vs adaptive sampling; cost vs signal tradeoff.
- Storage window for raw sampled invocations for enterprise customers (should we offer configurable retention as an add-on?).
- How much of the simulation logic lives in the analytics pipeline vs client-side approximations? (API design trade-offs).
- UX for paid vs free-tier (hide customer_id by default for public tier?).

Next steps & action items (owners):
- Maya: wireframes -> Figma pages (initial) by 2025-09-22.
- Arjun: prototype heatmap canvas component in the console repo (spike) by 2025-10-06.
- Sofia: define backend sampling and rollup schema, write initial migration DDLs by 2025-10-01.
- Jonah: draft privacy/redaction policy for token snippets and review with security by 2025-09-30.

Backlog tickets to create now:
- CONS-4180: implement heatmap aggregation API (route/model/seq-bucket).
- CONS-4181: implement example-invocation retrieval with redaction + log link.
- CONS-4182: simulation microservice for batching/quantization deltas.
- CONS-4183: canvas-render heatmap component + compare lanes.

Notes for future research:
- Investigate whether prefix-KV caching patterns concentrate cost on early response tokens in LLMs with high system/context lengths.
- Evaluate UI mental models: heatmap vs sankey (we may add a tiny sankey overlay for attribution to route-level cost).

If we want to demo this at the next product review: prepare 2 use-cases: (A) p95 regression in Route X traced to repeated tokens in generated summaries (show heatmap cluster), (B) quantization rollout for M-7b showing cost drop in the heatmap with diff overlay.

End of notes.
